ra: Sigurd is the central hero of the Volsung cycle (Byock, Saga of the Volsungs).
Brynhild is a principal figure of the cycle.
Fafnir the dragon is integral to the Sigurd legend.
Reginn the smith fosters Sigurd within the cycle.
Sigmund is a Volsung hero and Sigurd's father.
Signy is a Volsung in the early saga.
Volsung is the eponymous dynastic ancestor of the cycle.
Gunnar is a Gjukung within the cycle.
Gudrun is Sigurd's wife and a Gjukung within the cycle.
Hogni is a Gjukung within the cycle.
Wayland the Smith belongs to the broader Germanic heroic-legendary corpus.
Starkadr is part of the wider Germanic legendary tradition (Saxo/Gautreks saga).
Hervor belongs to the wider Germanic heroic-legendary corpus (Hervarar saga).
Ragnarr's saga is tied to the Volsung line via his wife Aslaug, daughter of Sigurd and Brynhild.
Sigurd slays Fafnir with the sword Gram, the cycle's defining deed.
Fafnir is killed by Sigurd.
Sigurd kills the treacherous Reginn after roasting Fafnir's heart.
Sigurd is betrothed to Brynhild before being deceived into marrying Gudrun.
Brynhild is Sigurd's beloved/betrothed.
Sigurd marries Gudrun under the spell of forgetfulness.
Gudrun is Sigurd's wife.
Brynhild is married to Gunnar after he wins her by Sigurd's disguised aid.
Gunnar weds Brynhild.
Sigurd is the posthumous son of Sigmund.
Sigmund fathers Sigurd.
Sigmund is the son of King Volsung.
Volsung fathers Sigmund.
Signy is the daughter of King Volsung.
Volsung fathers Signy.
Sigmund and Signy are twins.
Signy and Sigmund are twins.
Fafnir and Reginn are brothers, sons of Hreidmar.
Reginn and Fafnir are brothers.
Gunnar and Gudrun are siblings among the Gjukungs.
Gudrun and Gunnar are siblings.
Gunnar and Hogni are Gjukung brothers.
Hogni and Gunnar are brothers.
Gunnar and the Gjukungs conspire in Sigurd's murder.
Reginn incites the killing of his brother Fafnir to seize the hoard.
Reginn and Fafnir's family seizes Andvari's cursed gold and ring, the hoard Sigurd later wins (Byock, Saga of the Volsungs).
Fafnir broods on Glittering Heath over the cursed hoard originally extorted from the dwarf Andvari.
By slaying Fafnir, Sigurd wins Andvari's cursed gold and ring Andvaranaut, transmitting the curse through the cycle.
Odin appears throughout the Volsung legend (planting the sword in Barnstokkr, advising Sigurd, claiming the slain), linking the literary cycle to the Norse divine cosmos.
The Volsung line is descended from Odin via Sigi in the saga's genealogy (Byock).
Odin is the divine ancestor of the Volsung dynasty.
Starkadr is granted long life and martial prowess by Odin (and cursed by Thor), per Gautreks saga.
As a valkyrie Brynhild is one of Odin's shieldmaidens, put to sleep by him for disobedience.
Sigurd's dragon-slaying heroism is sometimes compared to the war-god Tyr's combat against Fenrir as parallel Germanic monster-fights; loose thematic alignment, not identity.
